title: Multiple Allelism & ABO Blood Group Genetics
quickSummary: ABO locus on Chromosome 9: 3 alleles (I^A, I^B, i). Genotypes = n(n+1)/2 = 6 possible genotypes yielding 4 phenotypes (A, B, AB, O). I^A and I^B are co-dominant, both dominant over recessive i.

conceptBreakdown.title: Multiple Allelism & ABO Blood Group Genetics

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Multiple alleles represent a population-level phenomenon where >2 allelic variants govern a single gene locus (n=3 for ABO on Chromosome 9). Total possible diploid genotypes = n(n+1)/2 = 6 genotypes resulting in 4 phenotypes (A, B, AB, O). IA and IB code for specific glycosyltransferase enzymes and are co-dominant with each other and completely dominant over i.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ABO GENETICS MATRIX
                           
   ALLELE      ENZYME PRODUCT                          DOMINANCE RELATIONSHIP
   I^A         N-acetylgalactosaminyltransferase       Completely dominant over i; Co-dominant with I^B
   I^B         Galactosyltransferase                   Completely dominant over i; Co-dominant with I^A
   i           Non-functional enzyme (No sugar added)  Recessive to both I^A and I^B
conceptBreakdown.content:
Human ABO blood groups are controlled by the **$I$ gene** (located on **Chromosome 9**), which encodes a glycosyltransferase enzyme modifying the oligosaccharide chain on RBC membrane glycoproteins.

### 4.1 ABO Genotype & Phenotype Matrix

| Genotype | Surface Antigen | Plasma Antibody | Blood Phenotype |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **$I^A I^A$ or $I^A i$** | Antigen A | Anti-B | **Group A** |
| **$I^B I^B$ or $I^B i$** | Antigen B | Anti-A | **Group B** |
| **$I^A I^B$** | **Both Antigen A & Antigen B** | **NONE** | **Group AB (Co-dominance!)** |
| **$ii$** | **NONE** | **Both Anti-A & Anti-B** | **Group O** |

### 4.2 Multiple Alleles Formula
- In a diploid population with $n$ multiple alleles for a gene locus:

$$\text{Total Diploid Genotypes} = \frac{n(n+1)}{2} = \frac{3(3+1)}{2} = \mathbf{6\text{ Genotypes}}$$

$$\text{Homozygous Genotypes} = n = 3 \quad (I^A I^A, I^B I^B, ii)$$

$$\text{Heterozygous Genotypes} = \frac{n(n-1)}{2} = \frac{3(2)}{2} = 3 \quad (I^A I^B, I^A i, I^B i)$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: The Bombay Phenotype (H-antigen Epistasis)
conceptBreakdown.title: The Bombay Phenotype (H-antigen Epistasis)
conceptBreakdown.content: Homozygous recessive mutation (hh) at the FUT1 gene prevents synthesis of H-substance precursor; even individuals with IA or IB alleles test phenotypically as Blood Group O because antigens A and B cannot attach.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Population vs Individual Allelic Scope
conceptBreakdown.title: Population vs Individual Allelic Scope
conceptBreakdown.content: While a population can have dozens of multiple alleles (e.g. self-incompatibility S-alleles in plants or eye-color in Drosophila), any individual diploid organism can inherit at most TWO alleles.
